title: With six or more members of one first name, the "Which one?" card offers only five and gives a wrong count
what: When more than five members fit the name the owner said, the card lists five of them and says that five members are called that name. The others cannot be picked, and nothing says there are more.
expected: The card says how many really match and lets the owner reach every one of them, or asks for the surname.
how_often: every time six or more members share the name asked for
fix_line: Say the true number and add a way to see the rest or to type the surname

title: When a save fails and the credit cannot be given back, the credit stays taken and the card can never try again
what: A credit is taken before the save runs. If the save fails and giving the credit back fails too (for example the internet dropped in between), the card shows only the failure, says nothing about the credit, and every later tap shows the same failure again without trying. After a reload the same card says it was done already, though nothing was saved.
expected: The owner is told that the credit could not be given back yet, the give-back is tried again, and a later tap is a real new try that takes no second credit.
how_often: rare: only when the give-back fails after a failed save
fix_line: Tell the owner, retry the give-back, and let the next tap run again

title: The "members by batch" answer shows the number of batches as its big figure under a heading about members
what: The card headed "Members with a running plan, by batch" shows the count of batches in big figures. The sister cards by plan and by men and women show the number of members there.
expected: The big figure is the number of members with a running plan, the same as on the sister cards.
how_often: every time the by-batch question is asked
fix_line: Show the member count as the big figure
